highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.232 Released
highlights.summary: Subagent forking is now on by default, meaning a 'fork' subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache for more consistent multi-agent workflows. You can now type '@' in the prompt to mention and reference another Claude session by name, making it easier to coordinate between parallel agent runs.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.233 Released
highlights.summary: GitLab merge request URLs are now supported in the '--worktree' flag and the 'claude agents' view, making GitLab workflows a first-class citizen alongside GitHub PRs. An opt-in 'forward_user_identity' setting was added for enterprise gateway setups, allowing proxies to receive signed-in user identity headers.

highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should be aware of this new model as it may become available as a backend option, potentially improving the quality of complex coding and reasoning tasks.

highlights.title: Maximizing the Value of Your Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Anthropic's official blog post shares strategies for getting the most out of each Claude Code session, covering topics like context management and prompt structuring. This is a must-read for developers who want to reduce token waste and improve the consistency of Claude's responses across longer sessions.

highlights.title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Claude Code has switched to 'auto' mode as the default, which automatically selects the most appropriate model and behavior for your task without manual configuration. Beginners will benefit most from this change as it removes a common point of confusion when getting started.

highlights.title: Show HN: Graft – Claude Code Hooks That Cut grep Tokens by 42%
highlights.summary: Graft is an open-source tool that adds Claude Code hooks to intelligently reduce token usage when searching codebases, claiming a 42% reduction in grep-related token consumption. If you're hitting context limits or high API costs during large codebase navigation, Graft could be a practical drop-in addition to your workflow.

highlights.title: Learn 80% of Claude Code in 10 Minutes (2026 Tutorial)
highlights.summary: This concise YouTube tutorial aims to cover the most essential Claude Code features in just 10 minutes, making it ideal for developers who want a fast, practical introduction without sitting through a full course. It's an efficient starting point if you want to get productive with Claude Code in VS Code quickly.

highlights.title: Vibe Coding Beginner Tutorial: Build Software by Talking to AI
highlights.summary: This Bilibili tutorial (originally in Chinese) walks complete beginners through the 'vibe coding' workflow — building real, runnable software by describing what you want to an AI, with no prior coding knowledge required. The creator distills four months of hands-on experience into a step-by-step demo covering how to write your first request, keep the AI on track, and push a project from idea to working app.

tips_of_the_day: Use the new '@' mention syntax in Claude Code v2.1.232 to reference a separate Claude session by name — this is especially useful when you have one agent researching and another implementing, keeping their contexts clean and linked.

Before starting a long Claude Code session, write a brief PLANNING.md file in your repo root outlining the task, constraints, and expected output. Sharing this file at the start of each session helps Claude maintain consistency and reduces the chance of it going off-track mid-task.

If your Claude Code sessions are hitting token limits during codebase searches, consider scoping your requests to specific directories or file patterns (e.g. 'look only in src/components') rather than asking Claude to search the entire repo — this alone can dramatically cut token usage without needing extra tooling.
